questions.q: What is an independent variable in a scientific investigation?
a: The variable that is intentionally changed or manipulated by the experimenter
The variable that is measured as the outcome
A factor that must be kept completely constant
The final conclusion of an experiment

questions.q: Which term describes the variable that is measured to see the effect of changes made during an experiment?
a: Controlled variable
Dependent variable
Independent variable
Extraneous variable

questions.q: What are controlled variables (or constants) in an experimental investigation?
a: Variables that are changed randomly
Variables measured to test a hypothesis
Factors that are kept strictly the same to ensure a fair test
Errors made during measurement

questions.q: Why is it important to change only one independent variable at a time while keeping all other variables constant?
a: To make the experiment take longer
To save laboratory chemical supplies
To confuse students reading the report
To ensure that any observed change in the dependent variable is solely due to the independent variable, making it a fair test

questions.q: What is a hypothesis in scientific experimental design?
a: A proposed testable explanation or prediction for a scientific question or observation
A proven mathematical law that never changes
A summary table of raw data collected
A list of laboratory safety rules

questions.q: What is the purpose of including a control group or control experiment in an investigation?
a: To waste extra glassware
To provide a baseline comparison to prove that the independent variable caused the observed effect
To increase the temperature of solutions
To test a second independent variable simultaneously

questions.q: In an experiment investigating how temperature affects the rate of enzyme action, what is the independent variable?
a: The rate of oxygen gas produced
The volume of enzyme solution
The temperature at which the reaction is maintained
The type of glassware used

questions.q: If a student investigates how light intensity affects the rate of photosynthesis in pondweed, which factor should be kept constant (controlled)?
a: The species and size of the pondweed used
The light intensity provided by the lamp
The distance of the lamp from the plant
The rate of bubble production

questions.q: What does 'reliability' mean in the context of scientific data collection?
a: Getting consistent, repeatable results when an experiment is repeated multiple times
Measuring the correct scientific quantity
Using expensive digital balances
Writing long paragraphs in conclusions

questions.q: How can a student improve the reliability of their experimental results?
a: Change all variables during each test
Repeat the experiment multiple times (at least three trials) and calculate an average
Guess values that seem correct
Throw away data that does not match expectations

questions.q: What does 'validity' mean regarding an experimental design?
a: How fast the experiment can be completed
The total number of students in the class
Whether the experiment actually tests what it claims to test by properly controlling variables
Whether the equipment is clean

questions.q: What is a random error in scientific measurements?
a: An error caused by a broken instrument that is wrong by the same amount every time
Mistakes in writing down student names
Deliberate alteration of data numbers
Unpredictable variations in measurements caused by factors like human reaction time or reading fluctuations

questions.q: What is a systematic error in an experiment?
a: A consistent error caused by poorly calibrated equipment or a flawed experimental method, affecting all readings by a similar amount
Random mistakes made while counting bubbles
Accidental dropping of test tubes
Variations in room temperature

questions.q: Why should an investigator record both raw data and processed data in data tables?
a: To create more paperwork
To allow verification of calculations and transparency in how conclusions were reached
To hide incorrect measurements
To make tables look colorful

questions.q: When designing a table for recording scientific data, what must be included at the top of each data column?
a: Random numbers and symbols
Student grades and ages
The name of the variable and its appropriate units of measurement
Drawings of the apparatus

questions.q: On which axis of a line graph is the independent variable traditionally plotted?
a: The vertical y-axis
The top margin
The diagonal axis
The horizontal x-axis

questions.q: On which axis of a line graph is the dependent variable traditionally plotted?
a: The vertical y-axis
The horizontal x-axis
The bottom corner
The center origin

questions.q: When should a bar chart or column graph be used instead of a continuous line graph to display data?
a: When both variables are continuous numerical numbers
When the independent variable is categorical (grouped into distinct groups like plant species or types of fertilizer)
When measuring time over a continuous period
When data has no numerical value at all

questions.q: What is an anomalous result (outlier) in a set of experimental data?
a: The exact average of all collected trials
The most common measurement
A data point that does not fit the general trend or pattern of the rest of the results
The highest value recorded

questions.q: What is the correct action to take when an anomalous result is identified in a set of repeated trials?
a: Ignore it completely and pretend it never happened
Change the number to match other data points
Include it in the average calculation without checking
Investigate the cause, repeat the measurement if possible, and exclude it from calculated averages

questions.q: What is the formula for calculating the mean (average) of a set of numerical data trials?
a: Sum of all values divided by the number of trials
Highest value minus the lowest value
Multiply all trial values together
Add all values and subtract the middle value

questions.q: Why is calculating a mean from repeated trials better than relying on a single measurement?
a: It guarantees there are zero errors in the experiment
It reduces the impact of random errors and provides a more accurate representative value
It makes calculations take longer
It increases the range of values

questions.q: What does the 'range' of a set of numerical data represent?
a: The average of all recorded numbers
The most frequently occurring value
The spread of data from the lowest value to the highest value
The total number of trials conducted

questions.q: What is a preliminary trial (pilot study) used for in experimental planning?
a: To write the final exam questions
To grade student lab reports
To clean dirty glassware
To test the method, identify suitable ranges for the independent variable, and check if equipment works

questions.q: In an experiment testing the effect of salt concentration on osmosis in potato cylinders, what is the dependent variable?
a: The percentage change in mass or length of the potato cylinders
The concentration of salt solution in the beakers
The initial mass of the potato pieces
The time left in the solution

questions.q: Why are potato cylinders blotted dry with paper towel before measuring their final mass in osmosis experiments?
a: To clean off toxic chemicals
To remove excess surface liquid so that only internal mass changes are measured accurately
To warm up the potato cells
To make them easier to cut with a scalpel

questions.q: What is the purpose of writing a step-by-step method before starting a practical investigation?
a: To keep desks tidy
To make the notebook look artistic
To ensure safety, organization, reproducibility, and clear identification of variables
To test typing speed

questions.q: What is a conclusion in a scientific investigation report?
a: A list of equipment used
A description of safety hazards
A guess about tomorrow's weather
A summary statement explaining what the results show, referencing trends and whether the hypothesis was supported

questions.q: What does it mean to evaluate an experiment in science?
a: Critically assessing the method, identifying sources of error, discussing limitations, and suggesting realistic improvements
Complaining about the difficulty of the task
Calculating the financial cost of materials
Copying answers from a textbook

questions.q: Which of the following is a valid suggestion for improving an experiment where heat loss to the surroundings was an issue?
a: Use a stopwatch with higher precision
Insulate the beaker or test tube with cotton wool or polystyrene to reduce thermal energy loss
Stir the liquid slower
Increase the room temperature with a heater

questions.q: What is a categorical variable?
a: A variable measured in continuous numbers with decimals
The final calculated average
A variable that places data into distinct groups or names (e.g., color, material, species)
An error in measurement

questions.q: What is a continuous variable?
a: A variable that never changes throughout an experiment
A variable that can only be whole numbers like 1, 2, or 3
A variable that has no units
A variable that can take any numerical value within a range (e.g., temperature, time, mass, length)

questions.q: Why should axis scales on a scientific graph be linear and cover at least half of the grid area?
a: To ensure data points are spread out clearly and can be read accurately without cramping
To make the graph look colorful
To reduce the number of plotted points
To hide anomalous results

questions.q: What should be drawn to represent the general trend of data points on a scatter graph when there is a clear relationship?
a: A zig-zag line connecting every single dot
A smooth line of best fit (or curve of best fit) passing close to most points
A random square around the data
A horizontal line at zero

questions.q: What is the purpose of safety precautions in an experimental design plan?
a: To make experiments boring
To slow down practical work
To identify risks (such as hot liquids or corrosive chemicals) and specify protective measures to prevent injury
To comply with school uniform policies

questions.q: If an experiment investigates how exercise heart rate recovery time depends on fitness level, what is the independent variable?
a: The resting heart rate
The time taken for heart rate to return to normal
The type of stopwatch used
The fitness level or category of the participants

questions.q: What is an empirical observation in biological investigations?
a: Information gathered directly through the senses or scientific instruments during data collection
A personal opinion or emotional feeling
A fictional story about nature
A mathematical equation with no testing

questions.q: Why is it important to state units clearly in data table headers rather than next to every individual number?
a: To save space and make the data table clean and easy to read
Units are not important in biology
To confuse people reading the table
To make calculations harder

questions.q: What is a secondary source of scientific data?
a: Data collected yourself in the school laboratory
Your lab partner's rough notes
Data or information collected by other researchers, published in textbooks, journals, or reputable websites
An unverified rumor

questions.q: When writing an evaluation of an investigation, why is it important to distinguish between random and systematic errors?
a: Because both types of errors are identical in cause
Because it sounds impressive to examiners
It is not important at all
Because random errors affect precision and can be reduced by averaging, whereas systematic errors affect accuracy and require recalibration or method changes
